prd.problem: Movement and inspection must match the hex board: a unit turns to face the shared-edge normal before crossing each hexside, moves center to center through every hex of an accepted route, and selection uses the enclosing hex. Today motion.rs interpolates endpoint-to-endpoint with a single heading, and the frontend leaks opponent data: map.rs writes enemy hp into SVG <title>/aria-label text and view.rs renders any selected unit's supplies, CP and strength regardless of side.
prd.why_now: The prototype already finishes shortest-arc turns before travel with 18-view atlases (6x3 cells of 256 px, nominal 20 degree steps), but routed play needs per-edge legs, and L21 3.6 (Limited Intelligence, addition) makes privacy a rules requirement: 3.61 denies any knowledge of opposing counters except as expressly indicated, and 3.62 lists what is revealed (a stack may be examined on the map; combat reveals types/totals but not numbers; patrol, air recon, prisoners, construction, trucks/RPs and pilot ratings have specific limits). The four-orb split needs one route contract and one projection contract so animation and gameplay use the same steps and the same disclosed facts.
prd.users: Players issuing movement orders and inspecting friendly or enemy stacks on the campaign map.
prd.value: One movement orb owns route playback, orientation, selection/hover hex highlights and the inspection panel. Milestones: (E1) consumer fixtures and a pure route-playback model built on published map/simulation contracts; (E2) edge-normal turn-then-step playback; (E3) hex highlights and faction-safe inspection; (E4) integration with the simulation's real route results and viewer projections; (E5) browser acceptance with recordings and a DOM privacy scan. Owned files: crates/frontend/src/motion.rs, the movement/inspection modules created by the simulation scaffold split (crates/frontend/src/inspect.rs, crates/frontend/src/view/panel.rs) and src/styles/movement.css. map.rs internals and cna-map geometry stay map-owned (movement uses the MapOverlay API); catalog art loading stays catalog-owned; legality, costs, reveal timing and saves stay simulation-owned. Early fixtures let movement progress independently; final acceptance depends on upstream implementations, never the reverse.
success_metrics: Every played route is an ordered list of adjacent HexIds from the simulation; for each leg the unit finishes turning to the cna-map shared-edge normal bearing, translates across that edge, stops at the next center and turns before the next leg (unit tests on the pure model, browser recording inspected).

Geometric facing and sprite frame are separate: facing is one of the six edge-normal bearings published by cna-map; the frame is the nearest of the 18 atlas views, and the test table documents the per-bearing error (up to 10 degrees) rather than claiming exact art.
Playback consumes the simulation's ordered route, per-step costs, interrupt and reveal events; it never derives a shortcut from endpoints and never charges CP/fuel itself.

Friendly and enemy hover/selection use cna-map hit testing; the selected hex has a prominent outline, hover is visually distinct, stacked units are reachable, and neighbouring controls do not steal hits during pan/zoom.

Enemy stacks can be examined as L21 3.62 allows but cannot be commanded; detail panels, tooltips, SVG titles, ARIA text, previews and logs render only fields present in the viewer projection; a sentinel-value DOM scan finds no hidden enemy data.

Recordings and screenshots cover all six headings, a multi-turn route, seam wraparound (e.g. 350 to 10 degrees), interrupted playback, reduced motion, and selected/hovered friendly/enemy states at 2458x1358.
Movement leaves have only earlier prerequisites in the global DAG; no movement leaf blocks map/catalog contracts or simulation rules correctness.
out_of_scope: Creating historical unit identities or producing sprites (catalog).
Computing movement costs, legal paths, reaction windows, hidden information or saves in the frontend (simulation).
Generic fog-of-war hiding ordinary counters: L21 3.6 lets players examine any stack; limits apply to counter contents and specific events.
Claiming smooth walking animation from still direction frames, or synthesising missing headings.
Editing map.rs internals, cna-map, catalog modules or simulation crates; boundary changes go to the owning orb.
open_questions: 'Move through squares' is interpreted as traversing each adjacent hex of the accepted route, not introducing a square grid; this matches the supplied map and shared-edge requirement.

What exactly does an opponent see when examining a stack (L21 3.62 'Map: a Player may examine any stack ... what is in those counters is another story')? The simulation projection contract (cna-simulation E2.I1.S3) defines fields; movement renders only those.
Should stacks show counter backs/nationality colour only, or top counter faces? Pending simulation adjudication of 3.62 'Map'; fixtures carry both variants so UI work can proceed.

epics.title: Consumer fixtures and pure playback model

epics.user_value: Movement work starts immediately without waiting for the simulation's rules or the map's transcription.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures from cna-map and cna-simulation load in a dev-only playground.
motion.rs exposes a pure RouteLeg/PlaybackState model with unit tests; existing sandbox animation still works.

issues.title: Fixture adapter and playground
issues.summary: Load the map corridor fixture, route fixtures and projection fixtures into a dev page.
issues.approach: Dev-only route `?dev=movement` renders the corridor fixture via the MapOverlay API placeholder (or the legacy SVG until map E2.I2.S3 lands) and plays fixture routes.
risks: Fixtures may drift from contracts; pin contract versions and fail on mismatch.
acceptance_criteria: Playground loads all fixtures and asserts contract versions.

issues.title: Pure route-step playback model
issues.summary: Refactor motion.rs so playback is a deterministic function of route legs and time.
issues.approach: Keep existing Motion tests passing; add RouteLeg {from, to, bearing} and PlaybackState {Turning, Translating, Settled, Interrupted} sampled by time.
risks: Changing timing constants would alter the existing sandbox feel; keep 2 ms/degree turn cadence and 420-1800 ms travel unless E2 changes them deliberately.
acceptance_criteria: Model is DOM-free, deterministic and covered by unit tests.

subissues.title: RouteLeg and PlaybackState model in motion.rs
subissues.goal: Represent multi-leg routes as turn-then-translate segments.
scope: Add to crates/frontend/src/motion.rs: RoutePlayback::new(start_pose, legs, now) and sample(now, reduced_motion) -> Pose plus current leg index/state; legs take bearings as inputs (from cna-map), never compute them from pixel deltas.
Existing single-destination Motion API becomes a one-leg route; all current tests stay green.
acceptance_criteria: New tests: a three-leg route visits each center in order and never translates while |heading error| > 0.
All existing motion.rs tests pass unchanged.

epics.title: Edge-normal turn-then-step playback
epics.objective: Play accepted routes leg by leg, facing each shared-edge normal before crossing, with honest frame selection, interruptions and reduced motion.
epics.user_value: Units visibly drive through each hex of their route and face the hexside they cross.
acceptance_criteria: All six bearings, multi-leg and wraparound behaviour tested.
Frame selection table documents nearest-view error.
Interrupted playback stops at the interrupting hex center.

issues.title: Bearings, frames and interruptions
issues.summary: Use cna-map bearings, select frames separately, handle interrupts and wraparound.
issues.approach: Bearings from cna_map::geometry::edge_normal_bearing; frame = nearest of 18 views; interrupt = truncate route at the event's step index.
risks: Sideways VASSAL grids put bearings at 0/60/120... or 30/90/150...; use the constant from cna-map, do not hard-code.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover six bearings, wraparound, interrupts and reduced motion.

subissues.title: Per-leg bearing from cna-map edge normals
subissues.goal: Turn units to the true shared-edge normal for each step.
scope: Cross-project prerequisites (enforced by docs/planning/cna-dag.manifest.json): cna-map:E1.I2.S2 (edge-normal geometry)
Build legs from an ordered HexId route using cna_map geometry (center, edge_normal_bearing); reject non-adjacent consecutive hexes with an explicit error state (simulation bug, not silently skipped).
Cross-section seam steps use the canonical HexId and the shared edge from cna-map's seam table; check both center adjacency and that the travel segment crosses the shared edge perpendicularly.
acceptance_criteria: Table test for all six directions from a fixture hex: leg bearing equals cna-map constant exactly.
Non-adjacent input produces an error and no animation.

subissues.title: Nearest-frame selection decoupled from facing
subissues.goal: Keep geometric facing exact while choosing the closest available artwork.
scope: Use the existing directional_frame() with 18 frames; add a test table for the six travel bearings recording chosen frame and angular error; document in docs/movement/frames.md.
Atlas lookups go through the catalog inventory API (read-only); unknown atlas => fallback upright sprite.
acceptance_criteria: Error ≤10 degrees for every bearing and the table is committed.
Facing state stores the exact bearing, not the frame angle (test).

subissues.title: Interruption, wraparound and reduced motion
subissues.goal: Handle stops mid-route and seam angles correctly.
scope: Interrupt at step k: finish the current translation to hex k's center, then settle (never stop mid-edge); re-targeting during a turn starts from the visible pose; 350->10 degrees turns 20 degrees; reduced motion snaps to final state per leg sequence end.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: interrupt during turn and during translate end at the correct center; wraparound both directions; reduced motion produces no intermediate poses.

issues.title: Browser playback rendering
issues.summary: Render route playback on the map overlay.
issues.approach: Draw unit sprites in the MapOverlay units layer; sample RoutePlayback each animation frame; one opaque frame at a time (no crossfade).
risks: Frame loop must stop when idle to avoid battery drain.
acceptance_criteria: Playback renders correctly in the playground and is recorded.

subissues.title: Play authoritative route results with interrupts
subissues.goal: Animate exactly what the simulation accepted.
scope: Cross-project prerequisites (enforced by docs/planning/cna-dag.manifest.json): cna-simulation:E4.I5.S2 (ZOC interrupts in route results); cna-simulation:E4.I3.S2 (land movement costs and route producer); cna-simulation:E1.I1.S2 (npm run test:browser harness)

Consume cna-sim RouteResult (command id, game revision, ordered hexes, per-step CP/fuel, interrupt event with step index, ZOC/reaction stop) from the move command response; show cost labels from the result only.

Track the last applied event cursor/revision: repeated renders never restart a route, duplicate events never duplicate playback, an unaccepted or unrevealed suffix is never played, and tab-resume or reduced motion preserves event order.
